move: outgoing image smears left, incoming stretches in from right, hot seam
how: A canvas cycles three landscape images (aurora, ocean, sunset), each held about 1.57s with a slow push-in then transitioned in 1.1s, three times in 8s so the loop closes. During a transition, drawn column by column, the outgoing image is redrawn into a shrinking left region with a power-curve resample so its trailing edge stretches into a long smear (pull up to 8 at mid-transition on a sine), while the incoming image fills the right region with the mirrored curve; a white gradient seam glows at the boundary, peaking mid-wipe. The caption is pulled with the image: slides and stretches out left, then in from the right with the next name and index.
adapt: Replace the three images and names, change the count (the slot maths uses count times hold plus transition equals D), the smear strength 7 and seam colour. Keep the sine-shaped pull so the smear builds and releases.
port: mount(el, shot) creates the canvas and caption and loads the images; animate(el, shot, D) returns a timeline with one linear progress tween over D whose onUpdate runs frame() and positions the caption, replacing fx.register. Wait for image decode before the first frame.
caveats: about 1280 drawImage calls per frame during transitions
images must be reachable from the host; no getImageData so taint is not an issue
